reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 7 --verse 1.52.9: Sāyaṇa glosses bṛhat as bṛhatsāma, made by the praisers (stotāro yajamānāḥ) bhiyasā vṛtrabhayena, sense: afraid of Vṛtra they praised Indra with such a hymn; nṛṣācaḥ as prāṇarūpeṇa nṝn sevamānāḥ, which ‘attending on men in the form of breath’ carries. All three evidence pieces verbatim in the packet. The revision changes only the context clause (‘Telling of Indra’s fight with Vrtra, the hymn turns to the singers’ praise and the Maruts’ joy’) and ‘serving’ to ‘attending on’: day.js confirms hymn 1.52 is Indra against Vrtra (vv. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 15), v. 7 speaks of the hymns that magnify him, and Griffith’s v. 9 has the Maruts ‘joyed’; ‘Vrtra’ spelled as the app’s text; no four-word run from the key. Sāyaṇa takes anu amadan causatively (they gladdened Indra), but the plain sense follows Griffith and the reading does not claim the joy, so no drift. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.52.9, at [51,9]); entry-check ok, 45 words. 1.52 is not among the hymns where Sāyaṇa counts extra verses; Yāska does not treat it. No school, comparison or tone issue.
